title: What Happens When a Company Builds Its Own Team From Scratch
content:
###  **The Typical Timeline** 

Posting the role and interviewing candidates takes a few weeks. Training takes additional time before a new hire is truly effective. Then comes the wait to see whether they stay long enough to justify the investment. 

###  **What Often Happens Next** 

By the time a company has one or two consistent performers, months have often passed — and the season or opportunity the team was built for may have already shifted. 

###  **Why This Pattern Repeats** 

None of this is a reflection of poor management. It is simply what building a new operational function from nothing typically requires — regardless of the industry. 

###  **The Alternative Timeline** 

A structured program with existing training and supervision can begin producing consistent activity in the first week, without the months-long ramp-up.
